newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian opposition says no let-up for government.
newsitem.headline: Australian opposition says no let-up for government.

text.p: Australian opposition parties said on Monday they had no intention of letting the government off the hook in parliament just because it won decisively in a weekend by-election.
Prime Minister John Howard said after Saturday's electoral win in western Sydney that opposition parties should heed the message from voters and stop blocking government reforms.

Howard's coalition does not hold a majority in the Senate, or upper house of parliament, and key legislation, including the one-third sale of telecoms carrier Telstra Corp and changes to labour laws, are dependent on support from other parties.
"We don't usually do what we're ordered to by Mr Howard," said Vicki Bourne, a spokeswoman for the Australian Democrats. "We do what we think is fair."

The by-election result in the Lindsay constituency represented a swing for the Liberals of almost five percent on top of an 11.4 percent swing it achieved at the March general election that ended 13 years of Labor Party rule.
Labor treasury spokesman Gareth Evans said Labor would not be bullied in the Senate because of the government's win.
"Our position is absolutely justified and the measures that we will be opposing cry out to be opposed...," Evans told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio.
Senator Brian Harradine, one of two independent senators whose vote on the Telstra sale is crucial for the government, said the by-election would not influence him.

"I would be very loath to vote for any proposition which made it nigh impossible for a future government to buy back shares at a reasonable rate and thus repossess the natural monopolies," Harradine said.
Fellow independent Mal Colston has said his vote on the partial sale of Telstra remained dependent on an agreement from the government to protect jobs in rural areas.
The Greens also remain opposed to the sale of Telstra.
The government plans to raise A$8 billion (US$6.32 billion) from the one-third sale of Telstra, with A$1 billion earmarked for its environmental upgrade programme.
